issues_detected.description: Released-cohort size disagrees between sources (50,000 vs 'over 45K unique admissions'); the record chose the higher-tier figure and documents the choice.

The MIT License in external_resources applies to the GitHub software, not to the data; no data license or permission category exists. The record states this correctly, but the dataset's reuse terms remain unspecified.

semantic_insights: Description is quantitatively specific (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 imaging admissions, 23 Tb waveform, 14 of 20 centers) and internally consistent with instances, subpopulations and known_limitations.
NIH award OT2OD032701 (1OT2OD032701-01) matches the NIH OT2/OD pattern and the Bridge2AI Common Fund program named in funders, description and keywords.
Per-modality standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP schema) are stated consistently across conforms_to, conforms_to_standard, distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.

Access model (controlled enclave, registration, signed licensing agreement, notes retained on-site) is coherent across license_and_use_terms, data_governance, regulatory_restrictions, confidential_elements and third_party_sharing.
The record uses source_caveats systematically to declare what the sources do not establish (IRB, consent, HIPAA status, license, version, encounter date range) instead of asserting boilerplate.
Unit-mismatched counts (7,642 imaging admissions vs 1,000 de-identified images) are recorded as separate instances with an explicit caveat rather than conflated.

strengths: Quantitatively specific description and instance counts, with source disagreements documented rather than hidden.
Complete funding transparency: NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI with a well-formed OT2 award number, amount and period.
End-to-end technical transparency: per-modality raw sources, collection mechanisms, acquisition types, preprocessing, cleaning, labeling and named tooling linked to the chorus-ai GitHub organization.
Per-modality community standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, OHNLP) stated consistently across conformance, format and provenance fields.
Typed limitations and bias with mitigations, and a coherent controlled-access governance story.
weaknesses: No persistent identifier (DOI/RRID); id is a minted website fragment.
No IRB, consent or consent-waiver documentation for human patient data, including pediatric and neonatal patients, with at_risk_populations empty.
No data license or permission category; reuse terms rest on an unstated licensing agreement.
No version number, version access, errata or update schedule for a dataset that is explicitly still growing.
No variable-level metadata, no download or platform URL, no publisher, and no related_datasets (the holdout set is described but not typed as a relationship).
recommendations: Register a DOI (or RRID) for the released dataset and add a recommended citation.
Document the IRB of record, approval or exemption number, the consent-waiver basis for retrospective data, and protections for PICU/NICU patients under at_risk_populations.
State the de-identification standard applied per modality (e.g., Safe Harbor for OMOP, CTP profile for DICOM) and a residual re-identification risk assessment.
Add version, version_access, errata and an update cadence tied to the enclave releases; add a platform/request URL under download_url.
Publish a data dictionary (variables) at least for the OMOP tables and flowsheet extensions, and add prohibited/discouraged uses alongside intended_uses.
